$comment: THE CANONICAL CAPTURE INDEX for lifecycle-card evidence (cinatra#2821, epic #2784 S9h).
A cell name is a CLAIM. This file is where a claim is answered by a RECORD: the host the
picture declares, the URL it was taken on, the screenshot with its SHA-256, and the anchors
that were counted on that screen, in the frame they were counted in. The rules live in
scripts/ci/lib/capture-record-contract.mjs, and that module also exports the ONE path every
reader resolves. scripts/ci/chat-hitl-evidence-gate.mjs binds every acceptance-manifest cell
that names a host to a record here. An unindexed screenshot counts as zero.
THERE IS ONE OF THIS FILE, and it is read by BOTH gates. scripts/audit/chat-hitl-acceptance-gate.mjs
used to read a second index of its own beside it that also called itself canonical and held no
records -- and that empty one was the capture driver's default output, so an honest capture run
wrote where nothing would ever bind it. That file is retired; its load-bearing prose is the
C1 / C2 paragraph below. The audit half is the STRICTER reader: it adds painted counts, measured
absences, a pinned card instance and frame URLs on top of the contract above. Those extras are
GRADED WHEN PRESENT on a committed record and REQUIRED of what its own driver
(scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-driver.mjs) writes, so the strictness lands on the records
that tier makes rather than refusing eight records another honest driver made. The contract above
is the floor for every record either way.
FILE NAMES CARRY NO AUTHORITY. A cell called `__chat_thread__` whose record ended on a run-detail
URL, or whose chat anchors were never asserted, is a mislabeled capture and fails. A PENDING
capture owes its decision controls; a DECIDED one owes their ABSENCE and its own decided summary.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY IN IT, read off the records below rather than remembered: EIGHT records,
from three lanes, on two of the four hosts. Each group is ONE run of the recorder against a
LIVE app on a lane database, not a hand-assembled set:
A3 / A4 / A5 - chat_thread - cinatra#2855 (PR #2862), evidence/2855-settled-outcome.
A real gate PENDING, the same card SETTLED on its own floor naming its outcome and its
decider with no Refresh beside it, and one that LAPSED rather than being decided.
B3 / B4 - chat_thread - cinatra#2852 (PR #2863), evidence/2852-before-after. The re-shot
chip row in a real transcript: all suggestions accepted, then one chip dismissed, with the
count line in the decision floor in both. Their page_gate_region twins (B1 / B2) stay in
that lane's own capture-records.json, for the URL-class reason set out below.
C1 / C2 / C3 - site_widget - cinatra#2754 (PR #2870), evidence/2754-island-wire. The card
in the embedded conversation column on a genuinely cross-site host page, the same card
with the island expanded, and a NEGATIVE CONTROL with one character of the island
credential flipped. Each of the three was validated by capture-record-contract.mjs and came
back record/ok before it was written here.
This paragraph replaces three that had merged into each other and disagreed: two said the
file was populated and a third, left standing after them, said it was EMPTY ON PURPOSE. It
is not empty, and it has not been chat_thread-only since the C-series arrived.
MIND THE C1 / C2 NAMES. The site_widget C1 and C2 here are NOT the chat_thread C1 and C2 the
acceptance manifest cites from evidence/2573-s7-visuals-lane. Those two cells are still
UNBOUND and the gate is still honestly red for them. The S7 run observed THREE of the four
anchors a chat_thread record owes -- the /chat URL class, data-lifecycle-card-host=chat_thread,
and the card root, pending and decided respectively -- and never looked for
[data-conversation-list]. A record asserting a count for an anchor nobody measured is the
fabrication this index exists to refuse, so writing one would be inventing an observation
nobody made. Adopting the pictures above under their names, on the strength of a shared C1,
would be exactly the mislabel this index exists to refuse. They stay grandfathered findings
in the rollout policy until that re-capture happens.
THE page_gate_region RECORDS ARE DELIBERATELY ELSEWHERE, not missing. #2862 photographed the
review page's gate region once (A1) and #2863 twice (B1, B2); all three stay in their own
lane's capture-records.json. The contract's `review_page` URL class is /^\/agents\/reviews/,
while the shipped gate-region route is /agents/<vendor>/<package>/<runId>/review/<taskId>, so
a truthful page_gate_region record cannot satisfy the class as written. That is a defect in
the class, not in the pictures, and it is why the manifest's
`review-card__page_gate_region__pending` cell is unbound too.
A record is TEXT, and text is forgeable: a person can hand-write one with a real image and
invented counts. What the contract does catch is the accidental mislabel, the anchor nobody
measured, the drifted hash, the re-used picture, and the cell that cites nothing at all.

Not an error page, not a crash, not a sign-in form inside third-party chrome.

What ADJUST opens. It is a portalled Sheet OUTSIDE the card root, so this cell is full page; the row itself is untouched underneath.
